title: Break-Even Stretch

examples.explanation: The first five days add up to 3 - 1 - 2 + 4 - 4 = 0.
No stretch of days breaks even.

approaches.name: running total with the first index of each total

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Asks what to return when no stretch breaks even and whether a single day of 0 counts.
look_for: asks what happens if nothing breaks even
asks about a day with 0 change
hints: Before you start, is there anything about the answer you'd want to pin down?
Does a single day with no change count as breaking even?
Confirm that a stretch must be consecutive days and that nothing found means 0.

steps.title: Think in running totals
steps.description: Notices that a stretch breaks even exactly when the running total is the same before and after it.
look_for: mentions prefix sums or a running total
says equal totals mean zero in between
hints: Look at what a running total tells you about any stretch of days.
If the running total is the same on two different days, what happened in between?
A stretch sums to zero when the running total before it equals the running total at its end.

steps.title: Remember the first time you saw each total
steps.description: Stores only the earliest index for each running total, so stretches are as long as possible.
look_for: only stores a total the first time
uses a dict from total to index
hints: Check which index your code keeps when a total repeats.
To get the longest stretch, do you want the earliest or the latest day with that total?
Keep the first index of each running total and never overwrite it.

steps.title: Count stretches from day one
steps.description: Seeds the map with a total of 0 before any day, so stretches starting on day one are found.
look_for: starts the map with total 0 at index -1
tests a list whose prefix breaks even
hints: Try your code where the break-even stretch starts on the very first day.
What running total do you have before any day has happened?
Put a total of 0 at position -1 before the loop.

edge_cases.description: the best stretch doesn't start at day one

common_mistakes.description: doesn't seed the map with total 0 at index -1
common_mistakes.symptom: misses stretches that start on day one, like [2, -2]

common_mistakes.description: overwrites the stored index each time a total repeats
common_mistakes.symptom: finds shorter stretches than the longest

common_mistakes.description: checks every stretch with nested loops
common_mistakes.symptom: correct but O(n^2) on long histories

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you find the longest stretch that adds up to some target other than zero?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: running total with the first index of each total.
